**My thinking, as I sit here at the start of the season:**

I've been working this land for 40 years. My body knows the rhythm — wheat goes in the ground in October, maize follows in June after harvest, same plots every year. That's how I run 6 of my 9 mu. I've done this long enough that I don't need anyone to tell me when to water or how much urea to spread. I watch the leaves, I feel the soil.

My cotton — I keep 2 mu of it. I know some younger people around here have given it up. Too much trouble they say. But I know cotton. My hands know when the bolls need spraying, when aphids are coming. With two of my children working in the city now, I have fewer hands at home, but 2 mu I can still manage with my husband and whoever is around. I won't expand it. I won't cut it either. Cotton money is cotton money.

The last mu I put in mungbean. My family eats it, I sell a little at the market. It's easy. Doesn't need much from me — a little fertilizer, water it once when it's dry, pick off bugs once. That plot practically takes care of itself.

For fertilizer, I mix what I always mix — urea and compound fertilizer, amounts I know from doing this year after year. My maize gets the most because that's where the money and food comes from. Wheat I'm careful with in spring — too much and it falls over before harvest. Cotton I dose through the season, a little at a time.

Three irrigations for my wheat — before winter sets in, at jointing, then at grain filling. The well is close and works well. Maize I might only need to pump twice since summer rains usually help. Cotton I watch more carefully — drought stress during flowering kills yield.

I'm not changing much this year. There's no reason to.
